facts.state_of_play: Explosions reported in Kyiv after Zelenskyy warned of a Russian massive attack planned over several days; Russia has now struck Ukrainian cities with missiles, drones, and glide bombs, killing at least 10 civilians. North Korean ballistic missiles were used in strikes on Zaporizhzhia, killing seven civilian workers at the Metinvest steel plant and injuring 21; three more civilians including a 15-year-old boy were killed by Russian drones and artillery. Zelenskyy also warns Putin will use the Russian election — in which opposition to the war is banned — as a pretext for a major troop call-up. Russia's Supreme Court has now banned the country's only anti-war party from next month's parliamentary elections, the latest move to silence dissent. Ukraine is also targeting Wildberries, a Russian retail giant akin to Amazon, as part of an effort to bring the sense of war home to the Russian population. The Institute for the Study of War (ISW) warns that Putin is preparing to use this winter to break Kyiv, and will not enter serious negotiations if he believes he has a viable military path. Separately, Putin has ordered a probe following the humiliation of Russia's Navy Day parade. Russia has released former US Marine Robert Gilman, 32, after more than four years in prison; Putin granted a humanitarian pardon and Trump is credited with securing the release. The State Department stated explicitly that no prisoner exchange took place and Washington made no concessions. Fox News had framed the release as a prisoner exchange, which the US government has now denied. Gilman had been in a dissociative stupor for 47 days and was gravely ill; his father disputes the Russian account of his arrest. Trump has signed an executive order overhauling the childhood vaccine schedule, drawing pushback from doctors, pharma, and public health experts. A 7.4-magnitude earthquake — Colombia's strongest on record — has struck western Colombia, killing at least 240 people and leaving more than 3,000 missing; rescuers are racing to find survivors amid fears the death toll will rise steeply. A 32-year-old woman was pulled alive from a collapsed apartment on Tuesday, and footage circulating on social media shows a baby being rescued from the rubble of a destroyed building in Cali. The Trump administration has pledged $15.5 million in relief. Amid the earthquake aftermath, Colombia's new far-right President Abelardo de la Espriella, in office just over two weeks, has announced an immigration crackdown, ordering authorities to detain and deport migrants who are in the country irregularly or have committed crimes, echoing ally Donald Trump.

facts.state_of_play: Charges against ex-Olympian David Hearn and three other alleged vandals over the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool were dismissed after prosecutors found damage was caused by a botched contractor installation. Trump is pushing DOJ to open a new case — specifically exploring a misdemeanor prosecution — a request made one day after Todd Blanche was sworn in to lead DOJ. A Trump-aligned advisor publicly warned Pirro she has more than the Reflecting Pool to worry about. House Judiciary Democrats under Raskin have launched a probe and sent letters to both the Justice and Interior Departments demanding records. Pirro and Burgum remain subjects of that probe. Separately, DOJ has arrested Heidi Beirich, former SPLC chief financial officer, in California on charges of conspiracy to commit wire fraud, conspiracy to submit false statements, and conspiracy to conceal money laundering, alleging she oversaw a $4.1 million scheme funneling donor funds to informants inside white supremacist groups. Beirich's lawyer characterizes the case as an attempt to silence political opponents. In an unrelated action, DOJ released a report finding that guards at two California state-run women's prisons routinely sexually abused inmates and that the corrections department failed to provide safe reporting channels. California has been given 49 days to remediate conditions or face civil litigation; state officials say reforms are already in place.

facts.state_of_play: Trump's 'Economic D-Day'/'Operation Economic Fury' campaign against Iran continues nearing the six-month mark of the war, with the US reportedly facing diminishing stockpiles of key weapons even as it pushes economic pressure as an alternative to further military action. Vance describes the conflict as entering a 'new phase' centered on economic pressure. New US sanctions on Tehran are expected to be unveiled soon as Washington presses China and allies to join the campaign; Chinese analysts argue Beijing can resist by leveraging critical mineral supplies and its own oil reserves. The UAE, particularly Dubai, is seen as pivotal to the campaign's effectiveness. Iran's leadership, including President Masoud Pezeshkian, insists it is negotiating from a position of strength and claims the world acknowledges its victory, while other Iranian officials dismiss the economic threats as proof US military efforts have failed. Some reporting suggests US and global financial markets, rather than Iran, have been the first casualties of the escalating economic warfare. Separately, immigration authorities have detained family members of US military personnel, including the father of a USS Abraham Lincoln sailor, spotlighting a rising trend of ICE arrests targeting military families under the Trump administration.

Kyiv has now been hit by Russian drones for a seventh consecutive day, and fresh attacks on Kyiv and Odesa regions wounded at least 8 more civilians. This is in addition to the earlier large-scale Ukrainian drone assault on Moscow region and the deadly Russian missile strike on a Kharkiv region village. Additionally, a Russian 'double-tap' drone strike hit a shopping mall in Kryvyi Rih, Zelensky's hometown, killing 15-16 people and injuring more than 100, with a second wave of drones striking as rescue workers responded. A day later, further Russian strikes killed 6 more Ukrainians, while a Ukrainian drone strike on a home in southern Russia killed two children and injured their parents. German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul arrived in Kyiv by special train ahead of Ukraine's 35th independence day as Russia stepped up its attacks. The EU, Germany and France have now formally blamed Russia for a drone attack on Leipzig/Halle Airport, with Kaja Kallas calling it 'state-sponsored terrorism' and summoning Russia's envoy; UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband vowed Russia's attempts to divide Europe 'will fail.' Zelensky has urged airlines to avoid Russian airspace as Ukraine escalates its drone campaign and Russia vows to intensify strikes.

facts.state_of_play: Andy Burnham, now Prime Minister, faces scrutiny over an undeclared £6,600 Japan party from his time as Manchester Mayor. On his first foreign trip as PM, he traveled to Kyiv for Ukraine's 35th independence day, co-chairing a coalition-of-the-willing meeting, meeting Zelenskyy, playing guitar with Ukrainian soldiers, and announcing UK sharing of classified Storm Shadow missile-component technology and long-range missile blueprints, including support for France in setting up missile assembly lines, to boost Ukraine's missile production. Ukraine has reciprocated with a trove of secret intelligence data to help the UK train troops using AI as part of a landmark military agreement. Burnham has directly challenged Putin over the war's origins, asking 'Who started the fire?', amid Kremlin warnings that the UK is now 'participating in this war,' with a senior Putin adviser threatening a 'semi-military' response and possible attacks on UK drone factories, calling Britain 'evil number one' and declaring that 'Pandora's box has been opened.' Backbenchers have warned Burnham against calling a snap general election. Burnham says he is likely to travel to New York next month for the UN General Assembly, where he plans to meet Donald Trump and lobby, alongside other European leaders, for the US to supply Ukraine with Patriot missiles, calling the current supply problem 'fixable.' He has also said Prince Harry and Meghan's security arrangements are a private matter. Meanwhile, Zelenskyy says Russia plans to draft 300,000 more troops amid reports of increasingly aggressive and intimidating recruitment tactics as Russia prepares for a winter offensive, has warned on the prospect of wartime elections, and declared in a defiant independence day speech that Ukraine wants peace but will not give in to Russia at any price, as Ukrainian drones struck three major Russian retail hubs near Moscow, with Ozon identified as the next targeted economic pressure point, and attempted to strike a military cosmodrome; Ukraine marked the day with a parade featuring robots replacing soldiers. Moscow has since struck a cargo ship in the Black Sea after Zelenskyy called for talks to halt attacks, with Kyiv vowing to bolster regional air defences amid a renewed Black Sea blockade squeezing Ukraine's grain exports and farmers. Separately, the first British national is reported to have been killed fighting for Russia in a drone attack, and Burnham has signalled openness to cut-price tuition fees for EU students as part of a planned EU 'reset' summit. A key Ukraine ally was notably absent from the Kyiv gathering.

On Friday, Israeli settlers and soldiers killed two Palestinians in separate West Bank incidents: 17-year-old Karim Sanad Shalaldeh, shot by settlers, and 58-year-old Fathi Khazem, killed by Israeli forces. Video also emerged of Israeli soldiers themselves throwing belongings out of a besieged Palestinian home in Qusra, alongside settler sieges. Palestinian American homeowner Louai (Loui) Abo Ridi, back from Ohio after 10 days under siege, has directly confronted settlers outside his home despite Israeli military deployment, demanding protection from Israeli forces and the U.S. government. A new Yesh Din report finds settler attacks in Palestinian-administered West Bank areas have almost doubled since 2025 amid a self-proclaimed 'great settlement revolution,' with AJLabs analysis putting the rate at six attacks a day. Separately, settler children attacked a Red Crescent ambulance, the Board of Peace reversed course on a Gaza disarmament deal, Christian families report growing pressure to leave, and Israel opened tenders for over 1,200 homes in the E1 settlement, prompting France, Germany, Britain and Italy to join Europe and Canada in condemning the plan as making Palestinian statehood impossible. An Israeli minister also faces backlash over a gallows site with a 'viewing booth' for hanging Palestinians.

facts.state_of_play: IndyCar's Freedom 250 Grand Prix on Washington DC's National Mall concluded Sunday, marking the country's 250th anniversary and serving as the final major event of the celebrations; Kyle Kirkwood won the race (his second win of the 2026 season) after holding off the field, with Alex Palou starting from pole on the 1.7-mile street circuit. Trump performed a ceremonial lap in 'the Beast' before waving the green flag - initially struggling to hold it correctly until corrected by Melania Trump and Command Sgt Maj Matt Williams - then greeted drivers; DC Mayor Muriel Bowser served as grand marshal. Melania Trump attended alongside aide Natalie Harp and son Eric Trump, marking Melania's second public appearance this week. A scary crash occurred on Lap 36 when David Malukas clipped the inside wall and Sting Ray Robb T-boned his stopped car. Nolan Siegel, Marcus Ericsson, and Mick Schumacher had faced six-place grid penalties for engine changes. The event drew large crowds along a route past the Capitol Building and down Pennsylvania Avenue, with drivers reaching speeds up to 185 mph, though attendees faced logistical chaos including long water lines amid sweltering heat. The White House also faced online accusations of plagiarizing promotional graphics, allegedly resembling Rolex 24 race materials.

facts.state_of_play: Jury deliberations continued into a fifth day (Wednesday); after roughly 28 hours total, jurors sent a second deadlock note, prompting Judge William Sullivan to issue a rare Tuey-Rodriguez ('dynamite') instruction telling them a verdict is 'desirable' and ordering one final attempt. No verdict was reached by Wednesday's end, and a possible mistrial looms. Coverage also outlined the five verdict options available to jurors and highlighted renewed public debate over the adequacy of postpartum mental health care systems. Defense attorney Kevin Reddington has said Clancy is 'scared' as deliberations drag on. The killings occurred at the family's Duxbury, Massachusetts home; Clancy does not deny strangling her three children but attributes her actions to postpartum psychosis, while prosecutors maintain she knew right from wrong.

Nevada Gov. Joe Lombardo has declared a state of emergency, and the National Guard has been called in to assist firefighting efforts, with 800 firefighters mobilized amid shifting, unpredictable winds. Authorities have urged residents to prepare for a multi-day evacuation as winds are expected to worsen. The fire began Saturday in the Peavine Peak area of the Humboldt–Toiyabe National Forest near the California line, amid a weekend that also saw over 200 new wildfires erupt nationwide.

Separately, Fed Chair Kevin Warsh delivered a hawkish keynote at Jackson Hole warning that inflation progress is insufficient and the Fed 'may have work to do,' prompting investors to raise bets on a rate hike (including a possible September move), a jump in the 2-year Treasury yield, and mixed analyst reaction contrasting his clearer stance with a confusing July press conference. Commentary now frames Warsh's stance as risking a political clash with Trump, who favors lower rates, ahead of the midterms, while inflation pressures are also linked to the six-month mark of Trump's Iran war and a tariff dispute with Canada.
